sections.title: Tree and flowers
sections.text: Syzygium malaccense, the Malay apple, is an evergreen tropical tree usually 5–20 m tall. Its large opposite leaves are glossy; vivid pink to crimson flowers grow in clusters directly on older branches and the trunk, with many long stamens.

sections.title: Fruit and food
sections.text: The bell-shaped to oblong fruit is commonly 5–8 cm long and may be pink, red or purple. Its juicy, pale flesh surrounds a large seed; the ripe fruit is eaten fresh. Compared with S. aqueum, the Malay apple is generally larger-fruited, while S. jambos has pale, rose-scented fruit.

sections.title: Plate
sections.text: The plate's trunk-borne red flower clusters and red bell-shaped fruit match this species; flower colour varies among cultivated forms.
